lessons.key: ac_gap::when an ac requires surfacing a domain timestamp on a non happy path branch e g when something was previously done add that field to the response schema up front a short circuit that returns only the enum result silently drops it and nothing catches the omission until spec re verification
lessons.text: When an AC requires surfacing a domain timestamp on a non-happy-path branch (e.g. when something was previously done), add that field to the response schema up front — a short-circuit that returns only the enum result silently drops it and nothing catches the omission until spec re-verification.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a spec ac says the user selects from a list of external search results do not fold the search into the create submit endpoint and auto pick the first match expose a dedicated search list endpoint so the ui can render a real picker before the create action fires
lessons.text: When a spec AC says the user selects from a list of external search results, do not fold the search into the create/submit endpoint and auto-pick the first match — expose a dedicated search/list endpoint so the UI can render a real picker before the create action fires.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when a spec ac names a specific http status code for an authorization failure decide explicitly between role based denial 403 and ownership existence hiding denial 404 per case and reconcile the spec s wording with whichever is actually safer rather than leaving the two conflated under one status code
lessons.text: When a spec AC names a specific HTTP status code for an authorization failure, decide explicitly between role-based denial (403) and ownership/existence-hiding denial (404) per case, and reconcile the spec's wording with whichever is actually safer rather than leaving the two conflated under one status code.

lessons.key: gate_fail::when a test tampers a base64url encoded signature token to prove verification rejects it flip a byte in the middle of the payload or corrupt multiple characters not just the value s last character the last base64 group can carry unused padding bits so a single character flip there has a measurable chance of leaving the decoded bytes unchanged and producing a flaky false pass
lessons.text: When a test tampers a base64url-encoded signature/token to prove verification rejects it, flip a byte in the middle of the payload (or corrupt multiple characters), not just the value's last character — the last base64 group can carry unused padding bits, so a single-character flip there has a measurable chance of leaving the decoded bytes unchanged and producing a flaky false-pass.
